cfb.award_narrative.assessment: Measurement is a list of topics, not a calculation, and it includes an odds path (market-derived). Covered by the vote-share models; a market-free rebuild is production plus rank plus historical winner logit.
cfb.award_narrative.market_note: Odds path is a market-derived component; drop it and keep stats, team rank and historical winner logit.

cfb.award_vote_feature_model.assessment: Concrete spec but heavily overlaps cfb.award_vote_distribution; about 15 winners per award since 2010 cannot support a ridge multinomial with many features. Finalist vote shares are often unpublished except Heisman. Ballot-date as-of must be enforced per award.
raw_data: award winners and finalists by year
team record and AP rank at ballot date

cfb.ballot_points_gap.assessment: Garbled formula ('62 x 25 +...') and a softmax temperature fitted on about 50 events. Points and first-place votes per poll must be as-of the published release; revised or final-poll points leak. Endpoint field coverage unverified.
raw_data: weekly AP points and first-place votes by rank

sources.name: AP Top 25 poll archive (apnews.com, Sports-Reference polls)

cfb.ballot_points_gap.measurement_fix: For each AP release t record points P_i and first-place votes F_i for ranks 1-5 and voter count n_t (max points = 25 x n_t). share_i = P_i / (25 x n_t); gap_t = (P_1 - P_2) / (25 x n_t). Successor probability given the #1 team loses = softmax over ranks 2-5 of beta x (P_i / (25 x n_t)) with beta fitted by maximum likelihood on historical handovers where the #1 team lost (CFP era plus earlier polls, report the number of events). As-of the latest release published before the decision time; no revised data.

cfb.bowl_selection_state.assessment: Sound chain but selection score is undefined ('wins, rank and historical draw') and bowl list/tie-ins must be the contract-year table. Slot allocation order differs by bowl and year and is partly unpublished; APR fallback rule changes. Depends on simulation draws.
raw_data: bowl tie-in table by conference and year

sources.name: NCAA bowl lists and APR releases
Own computation from other catalog inputs

cfb.bowl_selection_state.measurement_fix: For each draw of cfb.rating_posterior_draws simulate regular-season wins; team eligible if wins >= 6, else if 5-7 included in an APR-ranked fallback list used only when eligible teams < open slots. Remove CFP field first. Allocate in bowl pick order of that season's tie-in table: each bowl takes the best remaining team of its tie-in conference by score = wins + 0.5 x (AP-ranked flag) + logit-fitted draw term (fitted on 2014-2025 bowl selections by multinomial logit on wins, rank, conference, travel distance). Output P(selected) per team and per-conference P(eligible < tie-in slots). Re-run weekly as-of latest results; no market input.

cfb.bubble_proximity_state.assessment: Overlaps cfb.poll_transition_model and cfb.poll_voter_behavior; the exact-rank CFP part ('density of resume gaps') is not a calculation. Others-receiving-votes points exist only in AP releases and are not in every API.
raw_data: weekly AP points for ranks 15-25 and others receiving votes

sources.name: AP Top 25 poll archive (apnews.com, Sports-Reference polls)

cfb.bubble_proximity_state.measurement_fix: At each AP release take points of ranks 20-25 and every unranked team receiving votes. For team i: z_i = (points_i - points_at_rank_25) / sigma_w, sigma_w = SD of week-to-week points change fitted on 2014+ releases for teams within 50 points of the cut; P(top 25 next release) = Phi(z_i + b x E[points change | result], opponent rank, margin) with E[...] from cfb.poll_transition_model. For CFP exact-rank use the committee rank model (cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model) predicted rank distribution and report P(rank = k) for k = 22..28. As-of latest release.

cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model.assessment: Reasonable spec; subtle points: committee releases since 2014 give only about 11 releases a year, strongly autocorrelated, so effective sample is small. ESPN SOR is a model output (not market) but is revised weekly; use the as-of vintage only.

sources.name: Own computation from other catalog inputs

cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features.assessment: Same committee-rank regression as cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model with the same features; only addition is a starting-QB injury flag and a hard-coded Nov 24 release date.

cfb.coach_buyout_exposure.assessment: Contract data is public only for public universities and via records requests; private schools (e.g. Notre Dame, SMU) are missing, so imputation drives many rows. Buyout step-down dates need contract documents; 'booster fund proxy' is not defined.
raw_data: head coach contract terms and buyout schedules

sources.name: USA Today college coach salary database
US Dept of Education EADA athletic finance reports

cfb.coach_exit_hazard_features.assessment: Honestly flags that 15-25 changes per year cannot validate a dozen covariates and falls back to base rate. Leak risks: buyout and outside-interest flags must be as-of the date they became public; coaches' 'announced' departures need exact timestamps.
raw_data: coach exit events with dates and cause

sources.name: USA Today college coach salary database
Own timestamped capture (news, depth charts, statements)
sources.note: must be captured live; no backfill

cfb.coach_overperformance_index.assessment: Sign convention is inverted ('expected minus actual') and mixes a projection with actuals; Coach of the Year winners are few (about 20 years) so the logit must be small. Preseason rating must be the pre-season vintage.
cfb.coach_overperformance_index.measurement_fix: Index = (actual wins to date + sum of remaining-game win probabilities) - (sum of preseason win probabilities over all regular-season games), where every game win probability comes from the frozen preseason non-market rating (SP+ or own, Week 0 vintage) plus site effect; add (AP rank at preseason - AP rank at ballot date)/25 and a conference-title indicator as separate columns. Fit historical Coach of the Year winners 2005-2025 with a logit on index, final record, final rank, first-year flag. As-of ballot date; no market input.

cfb.completion_yardage_profile.assessment: Air yards are not in the free CFBD data for most FBS games, so the proxy (YPC and 20+ rate) will usually be what is computed; the opponent adjustment and decay are specified. Charting sources are paid.
raw_data: pass plays with yards gained and receiver

sources.name: PFF College grades and snap data

cfb.conf_schedule_win_dependence.assessment: Well specified simulation; tau_c is an unfitted placeholder but declared as to-be-fitted. Needs frozen schedule and rating vintage as-of date; depends on cfb.sp_plus vintage problem (CFBD SP+ is not a weekly point-in-time series).
raw_data: team rating and rating SD as-of date

sources.name: Own computation from other catalog inputs

cfb.conference_membership_and_schedule_m.assessment: Reference table rather than a signal; correctness matters (realignment dates, tiebreaker text per conference per year). Maintained by hand, so version by effective date and keep source URL.
raw_data: conference membership by season with effective dates

sources.name: Conference and CFP official websites and press releases

cfb.counting_stat_tie_mass.assessment: Valuable for $1/N settlement. Depends on the joint stat simulation; calibration to 2010-2025 tie frequency is only a handful of leaderboards per stat, so binomial error is large. FBS vs Division I scope must follow the contract.
raw_data: player season stats by regular season
historical leaderboards per conference per season

cfb.cross_game_residual_dependence.assessment: Sound and market-free (signed residual vs non-market expected margin). Requires conference offsets in the posterior draws; empirical check on postseason-only samples is small. Uses 'backed side' which is leg-specific, so output is a function of the pack.
raw_data: games: date, teams, conferences, final margins, neutral flag
own rating posterior draws with conference offsets

sources.name: Own computation from other catalog inputs

cfb.defender_production_profile.assessment: Pressures and pass-rush snaps are PFF/SIS-only; free data gives sacks and TFL, so the snap-rate denominators have to be estimated. The Poisson simulation overlaps cfb.stat_leader_field_simulation.
raw_data: defender sacks, TFL and pressures by game
opponent sacks allowed and pass attempts

sources.name: PFF College grades and snap data

cfb.draft_declaration_propensity.assessment: Mock-draft consensus is not a market price but can be revised after the event; use only timestamped boards. Under NIL/revenue sharing the compensation proxy is undefined, and new draft-declaration rules shift behaviour, so historical calibration is regime-limited.

sources.name: Own timestamped capture (news, depth charts, statements)
sources.note: must be captured live; no backfill

cfb.dst_td_propensity.assessment: Reasonable; lambda summation treats events as Poisson, and k = 40 INT shrinkage is in line with rarity. Kickoff-rule regimes (touchback to 25 rule) change return TD rates, handled via regime table.
raw_data: plays with interception, fumble, return, blocked kick and TD flags

cfb.end_regulation_decision_profile.assessment: Score-difference set '{-3..-1, -8..-1 requiring TD+2, 0}' is garbled and 'expected from a fitted decision model' has no stated features. In FBS ties lead to overtime so the tie-seeking is a specific small-sample behavior.
raw_data: play-by-play final 2:00 of Q4 with down, distance, score, timeouts, clock
cfb.end_regulation_decision_profile.measurement_fix: Situations: Q4 plays with clock <= 2:00 where the offence trails by 1-3 (FG ties), trails by 8 (needs TD+2), or the score is tied. Fit a logistic model on 2014-2025 of aggressive choice (go for TD / pass on 4th, no kneel) on score diff, time, timeouts, field position, down, distance. For each head coach compute observed minus predicted aggressive rate over the last 3 seasons, shrunk with k = 15 situations to the conference mean; z-score = shrunk excess / SE. Coach change resets to coordinator plus career data prior. As-of previous Sunday.

cfb.expected_possessions.assessment: Formula '3600 - stoppage-adjusted halftime-neutral time' is undefined and the +1 for no-huddle is ad hoc. Heavily overlaps cfb.drives and cfb.pace; kept because it is the possession-count owner.
raw_data: drive table with start/end clock, plays, yards, result
cfb.expected_possessions.measurement_fix: Per team: mean drive duration d (seconds, excluding drives that end a half or occur in garbage time) over the last 10 games with weight 0.8 per game back, shrunk to the FBS mean with k = 5 games. Expected combined drives = (T_eff) / (0.5 x (d_A_own + d_B_allowed + d_B_own + d_A_allowed)/2) where T_eff = 3600 seconds minus mean untimed seconds (stoppages and halftime excluded) fitted on the season clock regime, with the clock regime as a covariate and no-huddle rate as a regressor, not a fixed +1. Report mean and SD fitted on residuals. As-of last completed game.

cfb.fg_attempt_make_model.assessment: Same quantities as cfb.kicker (make probability by distance, FG attempt rate by field position, weather covariates). Only adds drive-crossing counts, which cfb.drives and cfb.redzone cover.
raw_data: field-goal attempts with distance and result

sources.name: NWS api.weather.gov forecasts
sources.note: forecast vintages must be captured live; free historical vintages are not available

cfb.first_drive.assessment: Thin: no window, weights, opponent adjustment method or definition of 'first drive' (first of game vs first of half). Small samples, strong dependence on toss outcome; overlaps cfb.script and cfb.opening_poss.
raw_data: drives table with drive_number, result, plays, duration
cfb.first_drive.measurement_fix: Define first drive as the first offensive drive of the game for each team. Per team over the last 2 seasons with decay 0.5 per season: rates of TD, FG, punt, turnover, other, plus plays and seconds per drive; opponent-adjust each rate by subtracting the opponent defence's rate on its first drives minus FBS mean; shrink with Beta/Dirichlet prior of strength 20 drives to the conference mean. Report rates and mean plays. As-of last completed game.

cfb.first_td_race_rate.assessment: Long but computable; mixes offensive hazard with DST hazard and OT mass. Opening possession order is only known at the toss, so kickoff-time vintage differs from earlier time; p(no TD) is a small tail needing calibration.
raw_data: scoring plays with time and drive index

sources.name: Own computation from other catalog inputs

cfb.fourth_down_aggression.assessment: Computable with a stated fitted baseline; coach-change resets are specified. The second component (clock burned when leading) is a separate quantity mixed in; keep both outputs distinct.
raw_data: play-by-play down, distance, yard line, score, time

cfb.futures_coherence.assessment: Built entirely from market quotes (sum of mids, monotonic constraints); measurement is a thin one-liner. Useful only as a benchmark of stale quotes, not a predictive input.
raw_data: Kalshi market mids by contract and timestamp
contract family map (sum-to-one groups, implication pairs)

sources.name: Kalshi public market API
sources.note: candles and orderbooks must be captured/backfilled with timestamps

cfb.futures_coherence.market_note: Inputs are Kalshi quotes (prices); no market-free rebuild exists, benchmark only.
cfb.futures_coherence.measurement_fix: For each season-level family at timestamp t: take mid = (best bid + best ask)/2 for every contract, S = sum of mids over the mutually exclusive set (title, conference champion, etc.), coherence error = S - 1 after fees; for nested contracts (champion <= finalist <= playoff) record every violation mid_inner - mid_outer > spread. Compare with the model probabilities from cfb.season_sim_distribution and store the residual per contract. As-of snapshot t; benchmark only, never fed to a market-free model.

cfb.g6_cfp_berth_count_model.assessment: Computable and states no market input. Subtle: the bid rule changes year to year (2026 format uncertain) and 'Pac-12' membership affects who counts; berths negatively dependent via slots. Overlaps cfb.season_sim_distribution/cfb.joint_path_event_model but is a specific count.
raw_data: remaining schedule and conference title game rules
CFP bid and seeding rule text

sources.name: Conference and CFP official websites and press releases
Own computation from other catalog inputs

cfb.garbage_time_scoring_profile.assessment: Thresholds (Q3 > 27, Q4 > 21) are flagged unverified; decay 0.5 per season with k = 100 snaps is fine. Overlaps cfb.blowout_management but defines scoring per garbage minute, which is distinct.
raw_data: plays with period, clock, score diff, offense

cfb.goal_to_go_run_pass_mix.assessment: Clear and computable. Subtle: score-state logistic coefficients quoted (0.10-0.15) are illustrative; output 'expected TD counts given total' needs the expected-TD input. Overlaps cfb.redzone only partly.
raw_data: plays inside opponent 10 with run/pass and result

cfb.governance_vote_count_state.assessment: Hand-coded, single-event input (CFP expansion decision) with a logistic form that cannot be fitted on one event; statements are subjective and timing is political. Only usable as a structured checklist.

sources.name: Conference and CFP official websites and press releases
Own timestamped capture (news, depth charts, statements)

cfb.half_to_full_transition_matrix.assessment: Complete and delegates the tied-half bucket to cfb.half_tie_conditional_win to avoid overlap. Second-half receiver is known only after the opening toss. Cells with large first-half leads have few games; shrinkage prior is stated.
raw_data: games with season, week, home, away, neutral

sources.name: Own computation from other catalog inputs

cfb.halftime_adjustment_differential.assessment: The description itself says most of the raw differential is noise; coordinator changes need manual capture and the restricted WP window biases EPA. Low expected value beyond rating gap.

cfb.joint_path_event_model.assessment: Specified as exact event counting in one simulation with MC SE. Quality depends entirely on cfb.rating_posterior_draws, tiebreakers and bracket rules; example events are contract-specific.

sources.name: Conference and CFP official websites and press releases
Own computation from other catalog inputs

cfb.leader_race_state.assessment: Self-described bundle of state and projection; the projection is redone in cfb.stat_leader_field_simulation which says it takes only current totals from this input. Redundant as a separate definition.

cfb.leader_scoring_persistence.assessment: Points per minute when leading by 14+ versus close is the same effect as cfb.garbage_time_scoring_profile and cfb.blowout_management, with a slightly different threshold.
raw_data: plays with period, clock, score diff, offense
backup quarterback and running back snaps

cfb.lower_division_game_margin_model.assessment: Shares the rating with cfb.lower_division_title_model and adds only the game layer; margin cap 35 vs the other input's 21 is an inconsistency to harmonise. D3 game data (stats.ncaa.org, d3football.com) is scrape-only and connectivity is weak.
raw_data: game date, home/away/neutral, team ids and division, final score including overtime, playoff round and seed since 2010

cfb.lower_division_title_model.assessment: Conflicts with cfb.lower_division_game_margin_model on margin cap (21 vs 35) and rating method (Elo vs ridge), so two ratings would exist. Ivy tie handling hinges on unread contract text.
raw_data: FCS, D3 and Ivy game results
FCS playoff bracket and seeds by season

sources.name: Own computation from other catalog inputs

cfb.lower_division_title_model.measurement_fix: Use the single score-based rating of cfb.lower_division_game_margin_model (ridge margin rating per division, margin cap 35, home edge fitted, game weight halving each 1.5 seasons, preseason = 0.6 x prior final shrunk to conference mean) with its posterior SD. Simulate 20,000 seasons: remaining conference games, then conference title by that conference's tiebreak rule (Ivy: best conference record, ties shared and reported as co-champion), then the FCS playoff bracket from announced seeds with neutral/home site per round. Output P(champion) and P(co-champion) per team. Weekly as-of last completed game; no market input.

cfb.margin_total_joint_pmf.assessment: Non-market expected margin and total define the bins; strike points are contract terms, not prices. Bin counts (3x5) over about 10 seasons are adequate with the stated prior. Overlaps cfb.team_pair_score_covariance.
raw_data: games: final score each team, OT flag
own expected margin and total vintages

sources.name: Own computation from other catalog inputs

cfb.market_ratings.assessment: Entirely derived from closing spreads/totals; definition is computable (ridge Bradley-Terry with home edge). Benchmark only; must be tied to the lineup assumed by the line.
raw_data: closing spreads and totals by game

sources.name: ESPN public JSON odds
sources.note: odds fields inconsistent and often missing

cfb.market_ratings.market_note: Rating is the inversion of closing spreads and totals, market-derived by construction; benchmark for model comparison only, no market-free rebuild.

cfb.mismatch_cover_curve.assessment: Clear empirical survival curve with beta prior; rating gap non-market. Very large gaps (30+) have few games per bucket, so isotonic smoothing matters. FCS opponents need separate curve as stated.

sources.name: Own computation from other catalog inputs

cfb.net_yards_per_play_model.assessment: Parenthetical about sack accounting is confused: under NCAA rules a sack counts as a rushing attempt with negative rushing yards, so total yards are unaffected but rush attempts and rush ypc change. Fix the definition.
cfb.net_yards_per_play_model.measurement_fix: Per team: NCAA accounting where sack plays count as rush attempts with negative yards and kneels count as rushes. Expected plays N (from pace inputs), pass share p from script-adjusted attempts; E[yards] = N x [(1-p) x rush_ypa_adj + p x pass_ypa_adj], where rush_ypa includes sack and kneel yardage and pass_ypa excludes sacks (per NCAA pass attempt definition), each opponent-adjusted by the opposing allowed values over the last 10 games with 0.8 decay and k = 6 games shrinkage. Dispersion from historical residuals by bucket. As-of last game.

cfb.next_coach_candidate_model.assessment: Needs timestamped credible reports captured live; reliability weights from past hits are small-sample. Candidate pool defined ex ante to avoid hindsight leakage. Timing hazard from vacancy history is computable.

sources.name: Own timestamped capture (news, depth charts, statements)
sources.note: must be captured live; no backfill

cfb.nonoffensive_scoring_rate.assessment: Same defensive and special-teams TD rate as cfb.dst_td_propensity (interception, fumble, return, blocked-kick TDs per team-game with shrinkage).
raw_data: plays with type: interception TD, fumble TD, kickoff/punt return TD, blocked kick

cfb.opp_dropback_volume.assessment: Opponent neutral pass rate x expected plays x score state is exactly the other team's cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts; it only relabels it.
raw_data: plays with down, distance, score, play type, offense

cfb.ot_possession_scoring_rate.assessment: Computable; subtle: proxy from drives starting inside the opponent 30 is not the same as an OT possession from the 25, and the rule from the third overtime (2-point tries) is excluded. OT sample per team is tiny, weight 3 is ad hoc.

cfb.own_drive_share.assessment: Drive share is about 0.5 by construction in FBS (alternating possessions); the variation is one drive per game, and it is already determined by cfb.expected_possessions and turnover rates. Low value.
raw_data: drive table with start/end clock and results

cfb.period_drive_clock_budget.assessment: Computable; end-of-period truncation constants (0.1-0.3) are loosely stated and need fitting. Overlaps cfb.expected_possessions at game level but adds period split for quarter contracts.

cfb.period_margin_lattice.assessment: Overlaps cfb.half_to_full_transition_matrix, cfb.quarter_joint_scoring_pmf and cfb.period_share_of_total; 'compound-Poisson centring' is not parameterised, and 29 margin values x bins x periods is sparse.

sources.name: Own computation from other catalog inputs

cfb.period_possession_allocation.assessment: Formula error: if the opponent wins the toss and defers we receive first, so the term is 0.5 x opponent P(defer), not (1 - opponent P(defer)); also the 'kick/choose end' options are ignored. Toss result is unknown until just before kickoff. Overlaps cfb.opening_poss.
cfb.period_possession_allocation.measurement_fix: Per head coach: P(defer | wins toss) over last 3 seasons, shrunk with k = 10 tosses to the conference mean (remaining mass = receive; ignore choosing the end). P(win toss) = 0.5. P(team A receives first) = 0.5 x (1 - defer_A) + 0.5 x defer_B, and P(team A receives second half) = 1 - that. Expected drives in quarter k per team = season mean drives per team x quarter share (0.24-0.26) with Q1 and Q3 adjusted by +0.5 drive for the receiving-first team (Q1) or second-half receiver (Q3). Record realised toss only after kickoff; before that use the probabilities.

cfb.period_share_of_total.assessment: Clear binned estimate with shrinkage; excludes OT. Subtle only that expected total must be the non-market one; overlaps cfb.q_scoring and cfb.half_split but adds conditioning bins.

sources.name: Own computation from other catalog inputs

cfb.period_total_dispersion.assessment: Specified with a left-tail calibration test, which is the right check. Overlaps cfb.quarter_joint_scoring_pmf (same compound model) but the pmf is output here by period only.
raw_data: scoring drives by period with points

cfb.player_participation_hazard.assessment: Base rate 'a few percent per game' is a placeholder and workload/prior-injury multipliers are unfitted. CFB has no official injury report, so availability labels come from news with timestamps and are incomplete.

sources.name: Own timestamped capture (news, depth charts, statements)
sources.note: must be captured live; no backfill

cfb.player_participation_hazard.measurement_fix: Fit on FBS 2014-2025 player-games: P(miss game g) = logistic(position, carries per game over position median (z), prior-season games missed share, previous-week missed flag, team games remaining) with a position-specific intercept from the data (no assumed constant); P(season-ending | miss) = fraction of misses followed by all remaining games missed, by position. Remaining-season path = Bernoulli chain over games remaining. Redshirt and transfer eligibility enter as absorbing states. Weekly update with news captured with timestamps; as-of previous Sunday.

cfb.poll_release_calendar.assessment: Reference table, not a signal; correctness of label-to-date mapping matters (Preseason unnumbered, Final after bowls) and CFP release dates can move. Easy to verify against archives.
raw_data: release dates and labels by season

sources.name: AP Top 25 poll archive (apnews.com, Sports-Reference polls)
Conference and CFP official websites and press releases

cfb.poll_transition_model.assessment: Same model as cfb.poll_voter_behavior (week-over-week AP rank transitions given result, opponent rank, margin, ordered-response fit); only adds random effects and a longer history.
raw_data: weekly AP rank, points, first-place votes

sources.name: AP Top 25 poll archive (apnews.com, Sports-Reference polls)

cfb.program_trajectory_index.assessment: AR(1) parameters 0.7 and 4 are labelled placeholders, unsourced and unfitted; revenue-sharing resources are not public. Four-season forecasts have little validation data.
cfb.program_trajectory_index.measurement_fix: Estimate by regression on 2014-2025 team-seasons: rating_{t+1} - mu = phi x (rating_t - mu) + b1 x (3-year recruiting composite z) + b2 x (net portal rating change z) + b3 x (new head coach flag) + e, with phi, b1-b3 and the residual SD fitted (report values and CI), rating = non-market SP+ or own. Simulate 4 seasons ahead from the as-of preseason rating; add coach-exit hazard and conference membership as stated. P(at least one CFP berth) uses cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model. As-of preseason, update after portal window.

cfb.pythag_luck.assessment: Thin: no exponent, window, regression factor or definition of PPA expected wins. No raw data listed. Overlaps cfb.turnover_luck as a regression-to-mean concept.
cfb.pythag_luck.measurement_fix: Pythagorean win% = PF^k / (PF^k + PA^k) with k = 2.37 (re-fit on FBS 2005-2025 by least squares on final win%); luck = actual wins - Pythagorean wins to date. Also one-score record (games decided by <= 8 points) vs the PPA-based expectation: sum of game win probabilities from opponent-adjusted season PPA margin. Shrink luck to zero with 50 percent regression for the rest of the season (fit the factor on season-split correlation of first-half luck with second-half win% residual). As-of last completed game.

cfb.qb_availability_hazard.assessment: QB case of cfb.player_participation_hazard (miss-game probability with workload and prior injury, 'few percent' placeholder); adding a backup rating does not make it a distinct quantity (the backup path is in cfb.qb_replacement_value).

sources.name: Own timestamped capture (news, depth charts, statements)
sources.note: must be captured live; no backfill

cfb.qb_interception_propensity.assessment: 'Conversion factor' undefined and turnover-worthy plays require PFF-type charting (paid). Equal weights 0.5/0.5 are arbitrary.

sources.name: PFF College grades and snap data

cfb.qb_interception_propensity.measurement_fix: Per QB: INT rate = w x realised INT per attempt (2 seasons, weights 0.6 per season) + (1-w) x predicted INT rate from a logistic on average depth of target proxy (yards per completion, completion%, sack rate) fitted on all FBS QBs, w = n/(n + 200) so weight on realised rate rises with attempts (k = 200). Where PFF turnover-worthy rate exists, replace the predicted component by turnover-worthy rate x fitted conversion (INT per TWP). Opponent defence factor = opponent INT rate over expected, shrunk with k = 300 attempts. Multiply by expected opponent dropbacks. As-of pregame QB status.

cfb.qb_replacement_value.assessment: '0.75 points per EPA-equivalent play' is unexplained: EPA is already in points, so multiplying by 0.75 double-converts. Starter value uses only 2 seasons, and depth-chart vintage is own capture.
raw_data: play-by-play with passer id, EPA, dropbacks

sources.name: Own timestamped capture (news, depth charts, statements)
sources.note: must be captured live; no backfill

cfb.qb_replacement_value.measurement_fix: Starter value = opponent-adjusted EPA per dropback (incl. designed QB runs) over the last 2 seasons with 1-season half-life weights, shrunk to a recruiting-composite prior (mapping of 247/On3 rating to EPA/dropback fitted on historical FBS QBs) with k = 150 dropbacks; the same for the replacement. Swap value in points per game = (starter - replacement) EPA/dropback x team dropbacks per game (35-45, from script inputs); no extra conversion factor. Report mean and posterior SD. As-of timestamp = last confirmed depth chart or beat-report vintage before kickoff.

cfb.qb_sack_proneness.assessment: Separating QB from line effect is hard with free data (pressures and time to throw are paid), so the decomposition leans on proxies. Spec is otherwise computable with stated shrinkage.

sources.name: PFF College grades and snap data

cfb.quarter_joint_scoring_pmf.assessment: Complete (NB drives, 3/6/7/8 mixture, Gaussian copula, 50,000 sims). High modelling load; overlaps cfb.period_total_dispersion but it is the full joint. Q4 regulation only for QHIGHSCORE.
raw_data: line scores by period for both teams
scoring drives by quarter with points

cfb.rating_posterior_draws.assessment: Defines a draw set (4000) with game noise; subtle: 'portal-churn inflation' is unspecified in size. Draw ID persistence is useful. Prior from last season must use that final rating, not an in-year revision.

cfb.rating_posterior_sd.assessment: Closed-form SD is a by-product of cfb.rating_posterior_draws; '2.5 by week 10' is an outcome not an input and the 0.3 pace term is an unfitted constant.

cfb.realignment_feasibility_state.assessment: Needs contract terms that are mostly confidential (grant-of-rights end dates are reported, not filed). Event frequency is low, so the logistic hazard is weakly identified; flagged unknowns handled.

cfb.regulation_tie_curve.assessment: Concrete GAM on |expected margin| and total with 15,000 games; ties are about 5 percent of games so bin counts are fine. Overlaps cfb.ot_model, but this is the computable definition. Needs a non-market rating (SP+ vintage caveat).

sources.name: Own computation from other catalog inputs

cfb.remaining_game_win_probabilities.assessment: Formula logistic(rating_diff/13.5 + site_effect) adds a point-valued home edge to a scaled logit, a unit error; mixing logistic with a normal-based posterior is also inconsistent.

sources.name: Own computation from other catalog inputs

cfb.remaining_game_win_probabilities.measurement_fix: For each team and each unplayed game: margin mean m = rating_team - rating_opponent + site_effect (2.5 points home, 0 neutral, -2.5 away; fitted per season) in points; P(win) = Phi(m / sigma_g), sigma_g = 13.5 points (game SD fitted on FBS 2014-2025), using non-market ratings (SP+ or own) as of the most recent Sunday. For uncertainty use posterior draws from cfb.rating_posterior_draws (draw-wise P). Output the vector and its Poisson-binomial win distribution; rest adjustment only for known byes.

cfb.scoring_trip_efficiency.assessment: Points per drive reaching the opponent 40 overlaps cfb.td_per_scoring_trip (TD per trip), cfb.redzone and cfb.drives (points per scoring opportunity).
raw_data: drive start/end yard line, result, points

cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts.assessment: Computable regression with stated window and shrinkage; uses non-market expected margin explicitly. Overlaps cfb.pass_rate and cfb.script but gives the contract-facing count.
raw_data: play-by-play with play_type, down, distance, score diff, period, clock

cfb.script_rush_attempts.assessment: Leaves sack convention 'to be verified'; under NCAA stat rules sacks count as rushing attempts, so this should be fixed, not open. Lead-effect +-0.10 is quoted rather than fitted.
cfb.script_rush_attempts.measurement_fix: Rush attempts = (plays - dropbacks) + sacks under NCAA convention (sacks and kneels count as rushes). Run share on neutral situations (1st/2nd down, score within 7) per team over the last 10 games decay 0.8, then lead effect from a logistic on plays fitted by score margin (piecewise at +-14), opponent run-defence adjust by opponent rush attempts allowed, shrink with k = 6 games to FBS mean. Add sack rate x expected dropbacks (sack rate shrunk with k = 150 dropbacks). As-of last game; no market input.

cfb.season_max_total_tail.assessment: Extreme-value fit on rare events (a few games above 100 in FBS history); extrapolation to K 120-160 depends on the threshold. Needs FCS-FCS and non-FBS games; data completeness from NCAA is not guaranteed.
raw_data: final scores with overtime periods by game 2005 onward

cfb.season_ot_exposure.assessment: Ambiguous: q is described as tie curve x geometric period-length without defining the event (at least k overtimes, k from the contract) and the hard-coded 9 comes from a specific contract.
raw_data: season schedule with game dates and divisions
cfb.season_ot_exposure.measurement_fix: For a contract 'some game reaches at least K overtimes' in scope S (FBS or all D-I): per remaining game q_K = P(tie after 60) x P(game lasts >= K OT periods | OT) with P(tie) from cfb.regulation_tie_curve and period continuation probability r (fitted on OT games, with a separate r from OT3 for the 2-point regime), q_K = P(tie) x r^(K-1). P(YES) = 1 - prod over remaining games (1 - q_K), or 1.0 if the current-season maximum is already >= K. Update weekly with the remaining schedule.

cfb.second_half_ot_spillover.assessment: Expected OT margin conditional on team is near zero by symmetry except for strength differences; the main value is variance, which cfb.second_half_ot_total_increment and cfb.ot_model already capture.

cfb.second_half_ot_total_increment.assessment: Computable with OT sample of about 1,000 games; scope flag per contract is essential. Overlaps cfb.ot_model on P(OT) but adds points pmf for the total.

cfb.snap_weighted_availability_loss.assessment: Uses questionable/doubtful probabilities, but college football has no official injury designations (see cfb.injuries), so the 1.0/0.5/0.15 mapping is unfounded; PFF grades are paid and positional points per grade are unspecified.

Own timestamped capture (news, depth charts, statements)
sources.note: must be captured live; no backfill

cfb.snap_weighted_availability_loss.measurement_fix: For each player i reported out or flagged: loss_i = P_out_i x snap_share_i x (value_i - value_replacement_pos) in points, where value is on-field PPA/EPA per play (or PFF grade converted by a fitted regression to points per game) and P_out takes the share of historical 'flagged' cases that missed the game, estimated per source type (coach statement, beat report, team release) from captured history, not fixed constants. Sum over players (offence and defence separately), with QB handled by cfb.qb_replacement_value. Timestamp every report; as-of pregame.

cfb.sp_plus.assessment: Thin; compares with a market-implied margin (market-derived component). CFBD serves SP+ mostly as end-of-season/by-year values, so weekly point-in-time vintages are not guaranteed and later revisions would leak the future.
raw_data: SP+, FPI, SRS, Elo ratings by team and week with capture timestamp
cfb.sp_plus.market_note: Comparison with market-implied margin is market-derived; the rating pull itself is market-free if the residual-to-market step is dropped.
cfb.sp_plus.measurement_fix: Capture SP+, FPI, SRS and Elo for every team every week at fixed times (Tuesday) and store with capture timestamp; use only the vintage as of decision time (no revised history, no end-of-season values for in-season games). rating difference = rating_A - rating_B + home edge (2.5 points, fitted); convert to expected margin by regression of historical margin on rating difference per rating system, and blend by out-of-sample weights. No market-implied margin is used in the market-free build.

cfb.stadium_wind_exposure.assessment: Needs archived forecast vintages 6 hours out, which are not freely available for 8 seasons; the forecast-to-observed ratio would have to be built from own captures or a reanalysis proxy. Station-to-stadium distance adds error.
raw_data: venue table with roof, orientation, lat/long

cfb.starting_job_loss_risk.assessment: Logistic with stated windows and shrinkage; outcome (starter changed) is clear for QB, less for RB1. Depth-chart snapshots must be captured pre-game; 'portal arrival' indicator requires timestamps.

cfb.stat_leader_field_simulation.assessment: Complete and the owner of the projection; scope (FBS vs Division I with FCS from stats.ncaa.org) must follow contract. Large number of dependencies (player_usage, dvp, script volumes) multiplies model risk.
raw_data: team schedules with season_type and week

cfb.state_dependent_pace.assessment: Shrinkage statement '0.5 shrink toward conference mean (k = 200 snaps)' is contradictory (fixed 0.5 vs k) and overlaps cfb.pace and cfb.script.
raw_data: play-by-play with period, clock, score, offense, play_type
cfb.state_dependent_pace.measurement_fix: Per offence: mean seconds per snap (clock elapsed between snaps, excluding two-minute drills, timeouts and the final 4 minutes of a half) in four score-state buckets (trailing by 9+, within 8, leading 9-16, leading 17+) over the last 12 games with 0.9 per-game decay, shrunk per bucket to the conference mean with weight n/(n + 200) (k = 200 snaps). Expected snaps = 3600 clock seconds adjusted for the season regime divided by the opponent-adjusted bucket seconds weighted by the expected score-state mix (cfb.script). As-of last completed game.

cfb.td_count_dispersion.assessment: Clear NB fit with bootstrapped intervals; regime changes (clock rules) shift counts. Overlaps cfb.player_stat_variance conceptually but is TD-specific.

cfb.td_per_scoring_trip.assessment: Computable with decay and shrinkage; definition of 'trip' (first down at or inside the 40) is explicit. Overlaps cfb.redzone and cfb.drives but with a different threshold.
raw_data: drives with start/end field position and result

cfb.team_pair_score_covariance.assessment: Residual correlation of own and opponent points by margin/total bins is equivalent to the joint distribution of margin and total in cfb.margin_total_joint_pmf (and the generic cfb.corr).

cfb.team_period_points_share.assessment: Computable and explicit that no price or line is used. Interaction with cfb.period_share_of_total for the game total is stated; the kickoff-receiver adjustment (+-0.5 drive) is ad hoc.

m.stat_source_mismatch.assessment: Thin, and the target (contract settlement source and lock time) comes from Kalshi contract metadata. Not predictive; it's a data-quality guard. Source mismatch between CFBD, NCAA and ESPN is real but infrequent.
raw_data: player and team stats for completed games from at least two providers
contract settlement source and lock time text
m.stat_source_mismatch.market_note: Uses contract metadata (strike, settlement source) from Kalshi but no prices; the mismatch rate can be rebuilt from CFBD vs NCAA vs ESPN alone.
m.stat_source_mismatch.measurement_fix: For every completed game and stat S in {passing yds, rushing yds, receiving yds, sacks, TDs, team yards}: pull the value from the contract's named source and from at least one other provider (CFBD, NCAA, ESPN), record mismatch = values differ, absolute and relative gap, by stat and provider pair, with lock time of the settlement source. Mismatch rate m_S = share of player-games with difference; flag a ladder strike if realised value is within the typical gap (95th percentile of |difference|) of the strike. Compute after each game completion; no price used.
